title: Beyond Marigold: Seven Flowers to Decorate Your Home This Diwali
excerpt: Lotus for a floating centrepiece, jasmine strung as a curtain, orchids on the dining table — Indulge Express lists seven flowers that widen the Diwali palette beyond the marigold garland.
body:
• Indulge Express's Diwali flower list names seven alternatives and companions to marigold: lotus, rose, orchids, jasmine, carnations, tuberose and chrysanthemums.
  • Each flower is matched to a job: a single lotus as the centre of a floating arrangement, jasmine strings as a flower curtain and natural room freshener, orchids as dining-table centrepieces.
  • Rose petals fill water bowls under floating candles and sit between alpona and rangoli; carnations add a colour break on tabletops in otherwise neutral rooms.
  • Diwali falls on November 8 — buy fresh flowers on November 6 or 7 so garlands, bowls and centrepieces are at their best on the festival day.

Marigold does most of the work in a Diwali home — garlands at the door, heads in the pooja thali, petals in the rangoli. This year, Indulge Express has listed seven other flowers, each with a specific decorating job, for homes that want a wider palette without abandoning the festival's look.

Lotus and rose: the water pieces

The list opens with the lotus: buy one fresh, make it bloom at home so it lasts longer, and set a single large flower at the centre of a floating arrangement surrounded by petals and candles. Roses work at petal scale — scattered to fill water bowls before floating candles are placed, or set between alpona and rangoli designs on the floor.

Orchids, jasmine and tuberose: scent and structure

Orchids, in multiple colours with a subtle fragrance, are the list's dining-table centrepiece: set column candles around a bunch, or place jar candles beside them. Jasmine — mogra — earns its place on scent: strings of it can hang as a flower curtain, petals can go in the prayer room, and a small quantity in each room works as a natural room freshener. Tuberose, sold as long strands of fragrant white blooms, is the vase flower of the list, used to build a mixed bunch and to set up a contrast against multi-coloured flowers.

Carnations and chrysanthemums: the colour break

Carnations are the practical colour pop: choose red, white or yellow to match the room's theme and set them on tabletops and coffee tables, particularly where the rest of the decor is neutral or white. Chrysanthemums close the list for daytime events — for an afternoon puja or house party, a bunch makes a statement arrangement on its own, or the flowers can be aligned along a rangoli.

Putting it together

The ideas combine well with the traditional base rather than replacing it. Floral guides for the festival commonly pair garlands at the entrance with floating arrangements and petal rangoli inside, mixing marigold with rose and chrysanthemum for colour, according to Floristique's Diwali arrangements guide. Keep the division of labour from the list: marigold for the door and the pooja, lotus and rose for water, jasmine and tuberose for scent, orchids, carnations and chrysanthemums for the tables — and buy on November 6 or 7 so everything is fresh for Diwali on November 8.
